messages:
anna.sre: Planning a rolling GPU reboot + capacity-drain for dedicated pools in eu-west-1 next Tue 2026-07-14 01:30-02:30 UTC. Purpose: apply driver security patch and validate node evacuation logic for Dedicated customers.

maria: Thanks -- will this affect hosted traffic too?

anna.sre: Short answer: targeted at Dedicated pools only. We'll cordon & drain dedicated nodes, run a reboot sequence with health checks, and only evict hosted or shared workloads if we detect scheduling pressure. Plan is conservative: 1 node at a time, 5m drain + 10m post-reboot health check, full pass expected ~45-55 nodes -> ~1h.

josh: Can we confirm eviction behavior for in-flight KV cache shards and long-running KV cache warms? We don't want excessive cache churn for customers on Dedicated.

elaine: Runbook note: Dedicated pool drains will try to migrate pods to other dedicated nodes in the same pool. If pool capacity is low, admission will deny new hosted pods but won't evict existing hosted pods unless OOM/pressure. We'll also tag each eviction with `reboot_job=2004007777` for traceability.

deploy-bot: maintenance job created: job_id=dedicated-gpu-reboot-2004007777, parallelism=1, estimated_duration=01:00, canary_nodes=2

infra-bot: Capacity check: eu-west-1 dedicated GPU pools currently report 18% spare node headroom; we can perform a 2-node canary. Also note: some pools are at 9% due to scheduled customer packs. Recommend running canary in pools with >=15% spare first.

anna.sre: Proposed cadence:
1) preflight: canary on 2 nodes in pool-a (2% of pooled capacity) for 30m including drain+reboot+post-health checks
2) if ok -> staggered linear rollout across pools with 5m observation between nodes
3) if any health checks fail -> pause, investigate, and potentially revert node to previous driver with rollback image.

ops-bot: Abort/auto-rollback triggers (automated): host-level pod eviction >3/min for >10m OR average pod restart rate >0.5% in dedicated pools for 10m OR scheduler pending backlog >500 for 5m. An incident will be opened if any of these fire.

maria: I'll attach dashboards: dedicated-node-drain-count, pod-restarts-dedicated, scheduler-pending, kvcache-eviction-rate. Setting alerts to match abort criteria.

josh: Runbook snippet for drain/reboot and manual rollback (for quick copy):
```
# cordon + drain node
kubectl cordon <node-name> --overwrite
kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# reboot via internal actuator
curl -X POST https://internal-actuator/nodes/<node-name>/reboot -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# post reboot health check
kubectl get pods -o wide --selector=reboot_job=2004007777
# rollback driver if node fails health checks
kubectl label node <node-name> driver=previous && kubeadm reset && apply-driver-previous.sh <node-name>
```

elaine: Who's on watch during the window?

anna.sre: I'll run the rollout. Maria will own dashboards/pager. Josh will own cache/eviction logic and be pager second. Elaine will coordinate with oncall and support-lead for customer comms.

support-lead: I'll stage a support note explaining the maintenance to Dedicated customers and include expected minimal impact language. We'll only send if we hit >10m visible degradation.

product-ops: Any contractual SLA notes? Some enterprise Dedicated customers have stricter windows - have we notified them?

anna.sre: Yes - we've already notified Dedicated customers with maintenance windows last month via the console notice. For any customer who opted for blackout windows, we will skip their pools (we have opt-out tags in pool metadata). If anyone wants to confirm a pool skip, DM me.

infra-bot: Canary job created: node_list=[eu-west-1-pool-a-node-12, eu-west-1-pool-a-node-13], job_id=canary-2004007777.

ops-bot: Reminder set: 1h before window and 15m before.

maria: Abort criteria restated for humans: persistent pod restarts or unexpected mass evictions. If abort -> stop job, mark remaining nodes as deferred, open incident, and run rollback driver.

josh: Suggestion: enable pre-drain KV prefix warmup for the small set of prefixes that are pinned to Dedicated (quick curl):
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api/kv/warmup -d '{"prefixes":["/dedicated-gen/"], "region":"eu-west-1"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
This should reduce cold-start hammer after migration.

anna.sre: Good idea, we'll add that as a pre-drain step for each node.

deploy-bot: Reminder: will post per-node status updates to this thread during the rollout.

support-lead: I'll standby 01:00-02:00 UTC to triage customer messages.

anna.sre: Final note: if any Dedicated app team wants their pool excluded, please DM before Mon 23:59 UTC. We'll post the canary node IDs 30m before start and the full per-node schedule before we begin. Thanks :white_check_mark:
